<a id="tools-what-if"></a>

### Simulation and what-if

Run simulations, estimate or control long batches, sweep a parameter and compare models or runs.

<a id="tool-cancel_run"></a>

#### `cancel_run`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Ask a background job to stop (checked between replications, and
while a large model is still being set up).

The replications already completed are kept and become a run, exactly
as when `simulate` is cut short: the result is marked truncated. Returns
the job snapshot; poll `run_status` until `state` is `cancelled`.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

The job snapshot, with the same fields as `run_status`; poll until `state` is `cancelled`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "job_id": "<job_id>"
}
```

<a id="tool-compare_models"></a>

#### `compare_models`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Compare 2–5 models or runs side by side.

Returns per-metric values (`metrics`, in `models`/`labels` order),
deltas against the first entry, and which entry is best per metric,
plus a Markdown comparison table. `labels` gives each entry's model
name (a run's cached `model_name`), parallel to `models` -- `deltas`
keys and `best` values use the label, not the raw id, unless two
entries share a name, in which case that label gets its id appended
to stay unique.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metrics` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `models` | array<string> | yes | — | — |
| `num_runs` | integer | no | `5` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `best` | object | yes |
| `deltas` | object | yes |
| `labels` | array<any> | yes |
| `markdown` | string | yes |
| `metrics` | object | yes |
| `models_or_runs` | array<any> | yes |
| `warnings` | array<any> | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "models": [
    "<model_id_a>",
    "<model_id_b>"
  ],
  "num_runs": 20
}
```

<a id="tool-estimate_runtime"></a>

#### `estimate_runtime`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Estimate wall-clock time for a simulation before running it.

Times a real pilot and extrapolates.  `workers` is taken into account
with a contention-aware speed-up: parallel replications on a large
model scale at roughly ``w / (1 + 0.25 (w - 1))``, not ``w`` (8 workers
measured 2.8x on an 8-core box).  Models of 1,500+ elements are piloted
at an 8,760 h horizon and the fit scaled, so the call always returns.

`importance` overrides the model experiment's importance setting for the
estimate. When importance is on, `seconds_estimate` is the TOTAL time
until the whole operation finishes: the baseline batch plus one batch
per block per variant kind. `baseline_seconds` and
`importance_seconds` show the split.

Returns {seconds_estimate, baseline_seconds, importance_seconds,
total_batches, importance_batches, importance_blocks, range,
per_run_ms, pilot_runs, estimate_seconds, cached, advice,
storage_bytes_estimate, event_log_bytes_estimate, storage_note}: the
last three say how much the run will write to disk (the availability
plot is sampled at the model's own interval on every run).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `importance` | string \| null | no | `null` | `none`, `improvement`, `risk`, `both` |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `num_runs` | integer | no | `10` | — |
| `run_length` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `workers` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advice` | string | yes |
| `baseline_seconds` | number | yes |
| `cached` | boolean | yes |
| `estimate_seconds` | number | yes |
| `event_log_bytes_estimate` | integer | yes |
| `importance_batches` | integer | yes |
| `importance_blocks` | integer | yes |
| `importance_mode` | string | yes |
| `importance_seconds` | number | yes |
| `per_run_ms` | number | yes |
| `pilot_runs` | integer | yes |
| `range` | object | yes |
| `seconds_estimate` | number | yes |
| `setup_s` | number | yes |
| `storage_bytes_estimate` | integer | yes |
| `storage_note` | string | yes |
| `total_batches` | integer | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "num_runs": 200,
  "importance": "both"
}
```

<a id="tool-run_status"></a>

#### `run_status`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Progress of a job started with `start_run`.

Returns {job_id, model_id, state, phase, setup, completed_runs,
requested_runs, percent, elapsed_s, wall_seconds, run_id, summary,
error}. `state` is queued, running, done, cancelled or failed. `phase`
adds what a running job is doing: `setting_up` while a large model is
prepared (`setup` then has `{stage, done, total, percent}`; it can take
minutes before the first replication, and `completed_runs` stays 0), then
`simulating`. Small models skip straight to `simulating` and `setup` is
null. `run_id` is set once the
batch has produced a run, and `summary` then carries the mean of each
metric. Jobs are in-process only -- after a server restart the run is
still in the workspace, the job id is not.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_id` | string | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

`{job_id, model_id, state, phase, setup, completed_runs, requested_runs, percent, elapsed_s, wall_seconds, run_id, summary, error}`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "job_id": "<job_id>"
}
```

<a id="tool-simulate"></a>

#### `simulate`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Run a simulation and return structured results.

`hierarchy` (a name or id) runs just that hierarchy on its own, its input
always available -- useful for checking part of a model. This is a port
extension, not a Raptor feature: the result carries an `isolation` object
(hazards at the boundary, the treatment applied to each) and must not be
read as a whole-model figure. `treatments` is `{deps: up|system|
refuse, pools: full|share|refuse, streams: keep|separate, items: {...}}`;
call `extract_hierarchy` with `report_only` first to see the hazards.

Long runs send MCP progress notifications about once a second and can
be cancelled by the client (the engine stops between replications).

Returns {run_id, model_id, model_hash, runs, requested_runs, truncated,
wall_seconds, summary, warnings, caveats}; `summary` has each metric
with min/mean/max/stdev/sem. With capacity analysis on, `summary` adds
Units_Produced, Mean_Flow, Mean_Capacity, Capacity_Weighted_Availability
(Mean_Flow / FlowGenerated: the delivered fraction, where Availability
only means some flow got through) and Lost_Flow.  `caveats` is the model-validation subset
of `warnings` (surfaced separately so a client can show them first).
The Markdown body is a table with units in the headers.

The model is **validated first**; structural errors are returned with
the issue list instead of running.  The run is estimated first and
refused with a clear message if the estimate exceeds `timeout_s`,
unless `confirm_long_run=true`.  `workers > 1` is faster but not
bit-identical to a sequential batch.  Leave `workers` out and a large
model (500+ blocks, events and nodes) run 20+ times uses several cores
(half the machine's, at most 8); the result reports the `workers` used
and `workers_auto`. Pass `workers=1` for the sequential numbers. This is
a server default only: the desktop app and the command line are unchanged.

`seed` (optional, non-negative) re-rolls the batch reproducibly;
leaving it unset keeps the engine's fixed seeds, under which the same
model and run count always return byte-identical numbers.  If a run is
cut short by `timeout_s`, `runs` is below the requested count and
`truncated` is true -- do not read a truncated batch as complete.

Capacity: delivered flow is limited by link `nom_flow`/`max_flow`
caps, and those caps only bind on links entering a node whose
unrestricted flow is off (`full_flow: false`).  A model with no such
boundary node reports no lost flow.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collect_events` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `confirm_long_run` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `date` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `hierarchy` | string \| integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `importance` | string \| null | no | `null` | `none`, `improvement`, `risk`, `both` |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `num_runs` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `run_length` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `seed` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `timeout_s` | number | no | `1800.0` | — |
| `treatments` | object \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `workers` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |

Parameter notes:

- `num_runs` — Defaults to the model's configured `NumRuns`.
- `run_length` — Defaults to the model's configured run length.
- `workers` — Defaults to automatic selection: 1, or for a large model run 20+ times, half the machine's cores (at most 8, at least 2).

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `caveats` | array<any> | yes |
| `display_unit` | string | yes |
| `estimate_seconds` | number | yes |
| `estimated_wall_seconds` | null \| number | yes |
| `isolation` | object | no |
| `model_hash` | string | yes |
| `model_id` | string | yes |
| `requested_runs` | integer | yes |
| `run_id` | string | yes |
| `runs` | integer | yes |
| `summary` | object | yes |
| `total_seconds` | number | yes |
| `truncated` | boolean | yes |
| `units` | string | yes |
| `wall_seconds` | number | yes |
| `warnings` | array<any> | yes |
| `workers` | integer | yes |
| `workers_auto` | boolean | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "num_runs": 200,
  "importance": "both",
  "seed": 7
}
```

<a id="tool-start_run"></a>

#### `start_run`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Start a simulation in the background and return a job id immediately.

Same arguments as `simulate`, minus the hierarchy/isolation and
importance options. Use this for batches that outlive one tool call (a
100-replication, 20-year run is tens of minutes): the engine runs on a
daemon thread, `run_status` reports progress, `cancel_run` stops it
between replications, and the completed run is an ordinary workspace run
(`run_id`) whose results `get_run_results`, `get_table` and `get_report`
can read.

The model is validated and the batch size checked *before* the job
starts, so a structural error is reported here rather than asynchronously.

`workers` defaults as it does for `simulate`: a large model run 20+ times
uses several cores unless you pass `workers=1`.

Returns {job_id, state, phase, setup, requested_runs, ...}. `run_status`
shows `phase` (`setting_up` while a big model is being prepared, then
`simulating`) and `setup` progress, so a long quiet start is not a hang.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collect_events` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `num_runs` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `run_length` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `seed` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `timeout_s` | number | no | `1800.0` | — |
| `workers` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |

Parameter notes:

- `num_runs` — Defaults to the model's configured `NumRuns`.
- `run_length` — Defaults to the model's configured run length.
- `workers` — Defaults to automatic selection: 1, or for a large model run 20+ times, half the machine's cores (at most 8, at least 2).

**Returns**

`{job_id, state, phase, setup, requested_runs, workers, workers_auto, ...}`.  Poll `run_status` for progress and the finished `run_id`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "num_runs": 1000,
  "workers": 1
}
```

<a id="tool-sweep_parameter"></a>

#### `sweep_parameter`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Simulation and what-if](#tools-what-if)

Sweep a parameter across values and measure the impact.

Works on copies — the original model is untouched.  `field` may be a
friendly field or an indexed form like `repair_params[0]`.  Each row
carries the `run_id` and the `runs` count that produced it.  Returns
{rows, monotonic, all_rows_identical, warnings} plus a Markdown table;
`all_rows_identical` is true when every row's metrics are bit-identical
(which cannot be told apart from "the value was never applied"), and
`warnings` says so.  `monotonic` looks at the first swept metric and
treats a flat or single-row series as monotonic; `all_rows_identical`
needs at least two rows.  Concurrent sweeps are serialised, so two in
one batch both succeed.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | string | yes | — | — |
| `metrics` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `num_runs` | integer | no | `5` | — |
| `selector` | string | yes | — | — |
| `values` | array<any> | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all_rows_identical` | boolean | yes |
| `field` | string | yes |
| `markdown` | string | yes |
| `monotonic` | boolean | yes |
| `rows` | array<any> | yes |
| `selector` | string | yes |
| `warnings` | array<any> | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "selector": "Pump",
  "field": "repair_params[0]",
  "values": [
    4,
    8,
    16,
    32
  ],
  "num_runs": 20
}
```

<a id="tools-diagram"></a>

### Diagram and annotations

Lay out the diagram, add notes and callouts, and render a picture.

<a id="tool-add_annotation"></a>

#### `add_annotation`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

Add a drawing annotation (text box, rect, ellipse or arrow).

Place it **next to an element or another annotation** with
`adjacent_to` (a block/node/event/hierarchy name or `Kind:id`, or
`Annotation:<id>` / an annotation's label) plus `location`
(`right`/`left`/`above`/`below`/`center`, default `above`) and `gap`:
it is anchored,
so it moves with the target when the target is dragged or
`auto_layout` runs. `center` puts the annotation over the target and
ignores `gap`. Or place it **by coordinates** with `x`/`y` (+ `w`/`h`):
in scene pixels (the default, what the GUI stores) or, with
`units="model"`, in the model's own coordinates (the numbers element
`x`/`y` use). `w`/`h` are scene pixels (a block is 108 x 46). It
inherits the target's hierarchy; set `parent` to draw it inside
another level.

An `arrow` connects two things by name: give `from_` and `to` (an
element or an `Annotation:<id>`), or the four coordinates
`x1`/`y1`/`x2`/`y2`. Each end is independent: name just one (say
`from_`) and give the other end as coordinates (`x2`/`y2`) to leave it
free. An attached end follows its target and stops at the target's
edge, not its centre.

`style` carries the cosmetic fields: `border_colour`, `border_width`
(0 = none), `line_style` (`solid`/`dash`/`dot`/`dash-dot`/
`dash-dot-dot`), `fill_colour` (null = transparent), `text_colour`,
`font_family`, `font_size`, `font_bold`, `font_italic`, `z`.
Returns {annotation_id, annotation, summary}.

For an arrow the parameter is spelled `from_` (a Python keyword
conflict); the stored `anchor` object reads back as `from`.  In a
`build_model` spec the same `from_` spelling applies.
Annotations exist only in `.rbds`; exporting with
`save_model_as(format="rbd")` drops them.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adjacent_to` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `from_` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `gap` | number | no | `12.0` | — |
| `h` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `kind` | string | no | `text` | `text`, `rect`, `ellipse`, `arrow` |
| `location` | string | no | `above` | `right`, `left`, `above`, `below`, `center` |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `parent` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `style` | object \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `text` | string | no | `` | — |
| `to` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `units` | string | no | `scene` | `scene`, `model` |
| `w` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `x` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `x1` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `x2` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `y` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `y1` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `y2` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `annotation` | object | yes |
| `annotation_id` | integer | yes |
| `summary` | object | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "kind": "text",
  "text": "Pump is the weak link",
  "adjacent_to": "Pump",
  "location": "above"
}
```

<a id="tool-auto_layout"></a>

#### `auto_layout`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

Re-arrange a model's diagram onto the shared layered grid.

Runs the same engine the GUI's Auto Layout button and .rbd save
normalization use: longest-path columns from the Start node(s)
(left = upstream), rows spread within each column, so no connector
runs through a block.  Positions are written back to the model file,
so a subsequent `render_diagram` reflects them.

Scope the pass with one of:

- `hierarchy`: a hierarchy name or id — only that level's elements
  are repositioned; every other level keeps its coordinates.
- `selectors`: names / `Kind:id` of the elements to move. Those
  elements are laid out in isolation and translated so their group
  centre stays where it was; neighbours outside the selection are
  untouched.

With neither, the home level is laid out (matching the GUI); pass
`all_levels=True` for every level. `build_model` already lays out by
default (`auto_layout=True`).

`direction` is LR/RL/TB/BT; `max_columns` wraps the flow after that
many series elements (parallel branches share one position) into a new
band instead of waiting for the canvas width. `spacing` scales every
gap (0.25-3; 1 = nominal, lower compacts, higher opens it up). `label_side`
places above/below labels on the left or right when the flow is
top-to-bottom (auto = right for TB, left for BT). Use the existing
View > Link style `orthogonal` setting (or `render_diagram`) for
right-angle links.

The collision-refining step has a time budget (30 s in all): a dense
model can otherwise take minutes. If it runs out, the layered layout is
kept with whatever refinement was done, and `refine_cut_short` says how
many levels were left less than fully refined (0 when none).

Annotations placed next to an element (`adjacent_to`, or an arrow's
`from_`/`to`) move with it; ones placed by coordinates stay where they
are in the model. For a whole-model layout the gaps between stacked
elements are first stretched so notes anchored `above`/`below` fit
(the elements either side move apart equally; nothing moves closer),
and a note that would still land on an element or another note is
nudged to the nearest clear spot; one a user dragged away keeps its
offset. Nothing else ever re-lays out a model: saving and exporting
keep the positions as they are.

With `max_columns` set, each link that runs back from one band to the
next is pinned as a straight line by two routing points (saved in the
model, `handover_points` in the result); the next auto layout of that
level replaces them, and any other routing points in the laid-out scope
are cleared (`handover_points_removed`). The GUI does the same.
Returns {moved, model_id, scope, elements_moved, annotations_moved,
handover_points, handover_points_removed, refine_cut_short}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all_levels` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `direction` | string | no | `LR` | `LR`, `RL`, `TB`, `BT` |
| `hierarchy` | string \| integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `label_side` | string | no | `auto` | `auto`, `left`, `right` |
| `max_columns` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `selectors` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `spacing` | number | no | `1.0` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `annotations_moved` | integer | yes |
| `elements_moved` | integer | yes |
| `handover_points` | integer | yes |
| `handover_points_removed` | integer | yes |
| `model_id` | string | yes |
| `moved` | boolean | yes |
| `refine_cut_short` | integer | yes |
| `scope` | string | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>"
}
```

<a id="tool-delete_annotation"></a>

#### `delete_annotation`

- **Kind:** destructive
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

Delete one annotation by id.  Returns {deleted: annotation id, kind}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annotation_id` | integer | yes | — | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deleted` | integer | yes |
| `kind` | string | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "annotation_id": 1
}
```

<a id="tool-list_annotations"></a>

#### `list_annotations`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

List a model's diagram annotations.

`parent` filters to one hierarchy level (the `parent` field, 0 =
home).  Returns {annotations, count}; each annotation gives
annotation_id, kind, parent, text, geometry and, for name-anchored
ones, its `anchor` (target/location/gap, or from/to for an arrow).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `parent` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `annotations` | array<any> | yes |
| `count` | integer | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>"
}
```

<a id="tool-render_diagram"></a>

#### `render_diagram`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

Render the model diagram as a PNG image.

`level` is a **hierarchy id**, not a depth index: 0 renders the whole
model (home level); to render inside a hierarchy pass its id, e.g. the
hierarchy `id=900` is `level=900` (read hierarchy ids from
`describe_model`).  Passing `1`/`2` is a common mistake and reports
the available ids.

`zoom_to` frames a **close-up** on one or more named/id'd elements
(block/node/event/hierarchy) **within the current `level`** (it does
not change which level is shown), padded by `margin` scene units — the
way to render a large model legibly in sections.  A selector is a
name, a bare id, or `"Kind:id"` (e.g. `"Block:3"`); a selector that
matches nothing, or a bare id matching two element kinds, is an error.
The structured result carries `px_per_unit`, `effective_label_px` and
`legible` (a heuristic: `effective_label_px >= 7`), so a caller can
tell whether the text is readable and zoom in further if not.

Returns image content plus structured {width, height, elements_drawn,
elements_in_view, px_per_unit, effective_label_px, legible, png_path,
resource_link}.  `highlight` outlines named elements (e.g. the single
points of failure).  `theme` is 'light' or 'dark'.
`routing` is the link style: 'straight' (default); 'angled' (a short
stub out of each port, then a straight run); or 'orthogonal' (right
angles only, steering round other elements). Blocks never move, and an
orthogonal link that cannot be routed quickly stays straight.
`include_annotations` draws the model's text/rect/ellipse/arrow
annotations (default true).

This is the only RAPTOR tool that returns a picture: results are always
Markdown/data.  The PNG is capped at 1600 px on the long edge and is
also written to renders/ in the workspace.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `highlight` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `include_annotations` | boolean | no | `true` | — |
| `level` | integer | no | `0` | — |
| `margin` | number | no | `12.0` | — |
| `max_px` | integer | no | `1600` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `routing` | string | no | `straight` | `straight`, `angled`, `orthogonal` |
| `theme` | string | no | `light` | `light`, `dark` |
| `zoom_to` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |

**Returns**

Image content plus `{width, height, elements_drawn, elements_in_view, px_per_unit, effective_label_px, legible, zoom_to, highlighted, png_path, resource_link}`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "theme": "light"
}
```

<a id="tool-render_diagram_svg"></a>

#### `render_diagram_svg`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

Draw one level of the diagram as SVG text, without Qt.

For checking layout, connections and annotations when `render_diagram`
(a PNG of the GUI canvas) is unavailable, or when SVG text is easier to
read than an image. It draws blocks, nodes (S/E, HI/HO, k/n), events,
hierarchy ovals, links with arrowheads and annotations at the GUI's
scene positions; `routing` is 'straight' (default), 'angled' (short stubs
then a straight run) or 'orthogonal' (right angles only, round the
other elements). Blocks never move; an orthogonal link that cannot be
routed quickly stays straight. It does not measure fonts (long names are shortened,
the full name is in each element's `<title>`) or show state colours.

`level` is 0 for the top level or a **hierarchy id** (not a depth).
`zoom_to` frames the named elements on that level, padded by `margin`
scene units; `highlight` outlines them. A selector is a name, a bare id
or `"Kind:id"`.

Returns the SVG in the text result (up to 200 KB; larger drawings are
only written to the file) and structured {svg_path, width, height,
elements_drawn, elements_in_view, links_drawn, annotations_drawn,
highlighted, routing, links_routed, inline}. The file is written to renders/ in the workspace.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `highlight` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `include_annotations` | boolean | no | `true` | — |
| `level` | integer | no | `0` | — |
| `margin` | number | no | `12.0` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `routing` | string | no | `straight` | `straight`, `angled`, `orthogonal` |
| `theme` | string | no | `light` | `light`, `dark` |
| `zoom_to` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `annotations_drawn` | integer | yes |
| `elements_drawn` | integer | yes |
| `elements_in_view` | integer | yes |
| `height` | integer | yes |
| `highlighted` | array<any> | yes |
| `inline` | boolean | yes |
| `level` | integer | yes |
| `links_drawn` | integer | yes |
| `links_routed` | integer | yes |
| `renderer` | string | yes |
| `resource_link` | string | yes |
| `routing` | string | yes |
| `svg_path` | string | yes |
| `width` | integer | yes |
| `zoom_to` | array<any> | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "routing": "orthogonal"
}
```

<a id="tool-update_annotation"></a>

#### `update_annotation`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Diagram and annotations](#tools-diagram)

Patch one annotation.

Accepts any style field, `text`, explicit geometry (`x`/`y`/`w`/`h`/
`x1`/`y1`/`x2`/`y2`, in scene pixels or with `"units": "model"`), or an
anchor via `adjacent_to`/`location`/`gap` (text/rect/ellipse) or
`from_`/`to` (arrow). Re-anchoring to another annotation uses
`adjacent_to="Annotation:<id>"` (or its unique label). Moving an
anchored annotation by coordinates removes its anchor, as dragging it
in the GUI does; `"anchor": null` removes it and leaves the annotation
where it is.  Returns {annotation_id, annotation, summary}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annotation_id` | integer | yes | — | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `patch` | object | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `annotation` | object | yes |
| `annotation_id` | integer | yes |
| `summary` | object | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "annotation_id": 1,
  "patch": {
    "text": "Updated note"
  }
}
```

<a id="tools-results"></a>

### Results and tables

Read, page, plot and export the numbers from a completed run.

<a id="tool-export_analytical"></a>

#### `export_analytical`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

Solve exactly, as `analytical_analysis` does, and write a spreadsheet.

`modes` (default `["reliability"]`): one or both of reliability and
availability, solved with the same settings into ONE workbook, a set of
sheets per mode (Summary, Elements with the importance measures, Curve,
Equation, Assumptions). Reliability-only settings (`at`, `times`, `bx`,
`tau`, ignoring repairs) apply to the reliability solve only.
`phase="all"` solves every phase of a phased model on its own, a set of
sheets per mode and phase ("Phase 2 Summary").

The file is `<model>[_h<hierarchy>]_analytical_<modes>[_all_phases |
_phase<N>].xlsx` (`.ods` with `file_format="ods"`, an OpenDocument
spreadsheet), e.g. `Plant_analytical_reliability_availability.xlsx`,
in `folder` (inside the workspace; default `Tables/<model>`). An
existing file of that name is replaced. Every other argument is as for
`analytical_analysis`.

Returns {path, modes, results: [{mode, phase, reliability |
availability}]}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `bx` | array<number> \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `dependencies` | string \| null | no | `null` | `up`, `down` |
| `equation` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `file_format` | string | no | `xlsx` | `xlsx`, `ods` |
| `folder` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `hierarchy` | string \| integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `ignore` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | `repairs`, `pm`, `spares`, `resources` |
| `ignore_repairs` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `importance` | boolean | no | `true` | — |
| `max_bdd_nodes` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `max_variables` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `modes` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | `reliability`, `availability` |
| `phase` | integer \| string \| null | no | `null` | `all` |
| `standby` | string \| null | no | `null` | `active`, `absent` |
| `tau` | number \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `times` | array<number> \| null | no | `null` | — |

Parameter notes:

- `at` — Defaults to the model's time-terminated run length.
- `folder` — Defaults to `Tables/<model>` when omitted. The file name adds `_h<hierarchy>` and/or `_phase<N>`/`_all_phases` for a hierarchy or phase solve; an existing file of that name is replaced.
- `modes` — Defaults to `["reliability"]` when omitted.
- `phase` — Defaults to no phase. A phase-dependent model is refused with "Choose one phase" unless you pass a phase number; `"all"` solves every phase.

**Returns**

`{path, modes, results: [{mode, phase, reliability | availability}], resource_links}`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "modes": [
    "reliability",
    "availability"
  ],
  "phase": "all"
}
```

<a id="tool-export_tables"></a>

#### `export_tables`

- **Kind:** writes
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

Write tables to files: CSV, text, or one spreadsheet.

`tables`: keys from `list_tables`; omit for the default set (all input
tables except the all-columns block table, plus every result table
except the long ones). Result tables need `run_id`.

`formats` (default ['xlsx']): 'csv' one .csv per table; 'txt' one
fixed-width .txt per table; 'txt_report' ONE combined text report;
'xlsx' ONE Excel workbook and 'ods' the same as an OpenDocument
spreadsheet: a Contents tab, a Run Info tab, a tab per table and a
Glossary, real numeric cells, filters, frozen headers and print set-up
(the End-of-Run and interim cost reports go beside it as .txt files).
Any combination.

`folder` is inside the workspace (relative paths resolve against its
root); default `Tables/<model>` (or `Tables/<model>_<run_id>`).
Existing files of the same names are replaced.

Returns {folder, tables, files: [path], resource_links}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `formats` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | `csv`, `txt`, `txt_report`, `xlsx`, `ods` |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `run_id` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `tables` | array<string> \| null | no | `null` | — |

Parameter notes:

- `folder` — Defaults to `Tables/<model>` (or `Tables/<model>_<run_id>` with a run).
- `formats` — Defaults to `["xlsx"]` when omitted.
- `tables` — Defaults to all input tables except the all-columns block table, plus every result table except the long ones.

**Returns**

`{folder, tables, files: [path], resource_links}`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "run_id": "<run_id>",
  "formats": [
    "xlsx"
  ]
}
```

<a id="tool-get_report"></a>

#### `get_report`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

Get a paginated report section from a completed run.

section: 'final_results', 'end_of_run', 'events', 'capacity', 'cost',
'weak_link', 'importance' (only when the run asked for it) or
'availability_plot'.  `run_number` selects one
replication where the section is per-run.  format: 'markdown'
(default) or 'raw'.  Returns {lines, total, next_offset, markdown};
`lines` never exceeds `limit` (≤200).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | string | no | `markdown` | `markdown`, `raw` |
| `limit` | integer | no | `200` | — |
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` | — |
| `run_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `run_number` | integer \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `section` | string | no | `final_results` | `final_results`, `end_of_run`, `events`, `capacity`, `cost`, `weak_link`, `importance`, `availability_plot` |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | array<any> | yes |
| `next_offset` | integer \| null | yes |
| `section` | string | yes |
| `total` | integer | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "run_id": "<run_id>",
  "section": "final_results",
  "limit": 200
}
```

<a id="tool-get_run_results"></a>

#### `get_run_results`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

One completed run as a single assessable bundle.

Reads what the run wrote: the metric means and per-replication figures,
the capacity summary, and the weakest elements (`weak_link`). Use it to
judge a run without paging through `get_report`, and `get_table` /
`export_tables` (with the same `run_id`) when you need a whole table or
a workbook.

`top` caps the weak-link list (1..100).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `top` | integer | no | `10` | — |

**Returns**

`{run_id, model_id, model_name, runs, units, metrics, capacity, per_run, weak_link, files}`.

**Example**

```json
{
  "run_id": "<run_id>",
  "top": 10
}
```

<a id="tool-get_table"></a>

#### `get_table`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

Read one table: its column headers and a page of rows.

`table` is a key from `list_tables` (e.g. 'inputs.blocks',
'results.summary'; result tables need `run_id`). Rows are returned as
lists in header order, as the model file holds them (text such as
"12.500000") or as numbers for computed tables. `limit` is at most 200;
use `offset` and `next_offset` to page. Returns {key, title, group,
headers, rows, total_rows, next_offset, notes}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` | — |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` | — |
| `run_id` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |
| `table` | string | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `display_unit` | string | yes |
| `group` | string | yes |
| `headers` | array<any> | yes |
| `key` | string | yes |
| `next_offset` | integer \| null | yes |
| `notes` | array<any> | yes |
| `rows` | array<any> | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `total_rows` | integer | yes |
| `units` | string | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "table": "results.summary",
  "run_id": "<run_id>"
}
```

<a id="tool-get_timeseries"></a>

#### `get_timeseries`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

Get time-series data from a completed run, for the client to plot.

series: 'availability', 'capacity' or 'cost'.  runs: 'mean' (default),
'all', or a specific run number.  points: max samples after decimation
(default 100).

Returns {t, values, runs_included, decimated_from, envelope?} plus a

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `run_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `runs` | string | no | `mean` | — |
| `series` | string | no | `availability` | `availability`, `capacity`, `cost` |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `decimated_from` | integer | yes |
| `envelope` | null \| object | yes |
| `runs_included` | integer | yes |
| `series` | string | yes |
| `t` | array<any> | yes |
| `values` | array \| object | yes |

**Example**

  "run_id": "<run_id>",

<a id="tool-list_tables"></a>

#### `list_tables`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Results and tables](#tools-results)

List the tables that can be read or exported.

Two groups: **Inputs** (the model's data: blocks, nodes, events,
hierarchies, links, spare pools, resources, triggers, phases, system
settings) and **Results** (a run's report sections, per-run figures and
capacity samples). Pass `run_id` (from `simulate`) to include a run's
result tables; without it only the inputs are listed and the result
tables are shown as unavailable.

Returns {tables: [{key, title, group, rows, available, reason,
default}]}. `key` is what `get_table` and `export_tables` take, e.g.
'inputs.blocks' or 'results.summary'. `default` is false for the long
ones (event log, end-of-run report, interim cost, all block columns).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model_id` | string | yes | — | — |
| `run_id` | string \| null | no | `null` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model_id` | string | yes |
| `run_id` | null \| string | yes |
| `tables` | array<any> | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "model_id": "<model_id>",
  "run_id": "<run_id>"
}
```

<a id="tools-meta"></a>

### Meta and documentation

Discover distributions and read the documentation the server ships.

<a id="tool-list_distributions"></a>

#### `list_distributions`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Meta and documentation](#tools-meta)

List every distribution supported by the RAPTOR engine.

Returns structuredContent.distributions: each entry has the integer
code used in .rbd/.rbds, a human name, the number of parameters
expected, the parameter names in order, valid ranges, and an example
mean/stdev computed at unit parameters (the engine exposes numeric
stats, not symbolic formulas).

Use this before setting fail_dist / repair_dist to supply the right
number of parameters in the right order.

**Parameters**

No parameters.

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `distributions` | array<any> | yes |

**Example**

```json
{}
```

<a id="tool-read_doc"></a>

#### `read_doc`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Meta and documentation](#tools-meta)

Read a documentation source as text (paginated).

`name` is 'rbds' (the `.rbds` format guide), 'rbds-schema' (its JSON
Schema; open_model, build_model and validate_model check files against
it), 'dependency' (the dependency tutorial chapter), 'mcp-docs' (the
human MCP setup guide), 'mcp-reference' (the generated catalogue of
every tool, parameter, return and example), 'mcp-guide' (the tutorial
chapter), a tutorial chapter stem like 'ch11-capacity', a chapter
title fragment, or a path under `docs/` or `new_docs/`.  `offset`/
`limit` page the lines (limit <= 400).  Returns {name, file,
total_lines, offset, next_offset, text}.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | `200` | — |
| `name` | string | yes | — | — |
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string | yes |
| `name` | string | yes |
| `next_offset` | integer \| null | yes |
| `offset` | integer | yes |
| `text` | string | yes |
| `total_lines` | integer | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "name": "dependency"
}
```

<a id="tool-search_docs"></a>

#### `search_docs`

- **Kind:** read-only
- **Group:** [Meta and documentation](#tools-meta)

Search the RAPTOR tutorial docs for passages matching a query.

Multi-word queries match passages containing **all** terms (so
"capacity analysis system capacity" finds the capacity passages, not
nothing).  Returns {results}, each {chapter, file, anchor, text,
score}.  Use `read_doc` to read a whole document.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Schema default | Enum / allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | no | `5` | — |
| `query` | string | yes | — | — |

**Returns**

| Field | Type | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | array<any> | yes |

**Example**

```json
{
  "query": "capacity analysis",
  "limit": 5
}
```

<a id="resources"></a>

## Resources

Resources are read with `resources/read`; templates take the arguments shown in the URI.

| URI | MIME type | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raptor://examples` | `application/json` | List bundled example models as JSON. |
| `raptor://models` | `application/json` | Index of the open models (model_id, name, counts) as JSON. |
| `raptor://runs` | `application/json` | Index of completed runs kept in the workspace (newest first). |
| `raptor://docs/{chapter}` | `text/plain` | Read a chapter of the tutorial book (new_docs/chapters/*.adoc). |
| `raptor://examples/{name}` | `text/plain` | Read a bundled example model as .rbds text. |
| `raptor://models/{model_id}` | `text/plain` | Read the live model as .rbds text. |
| `raptor://renders/{name}` | `image/png` | Read a rendered diagram PNG by file name. |
| `raptor://runs/{run_id}/{section}` | `text/plain` | Read a full report section for a completed run. |

<a id="prompts"></a>

## Prompts

Prompts are reusable starting points a client can offer as a slash command or template.

| Prompt | Arguments | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `explain_model` | `model_id` | Explain an existing model in plain English. |
| `improve_availability` | `model_id`, `target` | Propose and test changes that improve availability. |
| `new_availability_study` | `system_description`, `mission_hours` | Start a new availability study from a plain-English description. |

## Book and guide

The tutorial book has **24 chapters**; the MCP chapter is book chapter 23 of 24 (source `new_docs/chapters/ch16-mcp.adoc`).  The hand-written [MCP guide](MCP.md) covers install, client configuration, concepts and worked task recipes.

## Reporting problems

Open an issue at <https://github.com/openpowershift/RaptorStudio/issues> with the client, the tool call and the server's `--log-level DEBUG` output.  The tool list is a tested contract, so a change to it is deliberate and shows in the diff of this page.
